name: Subject-Verb Agreement
moduleIntroduction:
Welcome! This module is about Subject-Verb Agreement. This is the rule that says a verb must 'agree' with its subject in number. If the subject is singular (one), the verb must be singular. If the subject is plural (many), the verb must be plural.

Why is this difficult? In French, you often hear the difference in the verb ending (parle vs parlent sound similar, but est vs sont sound different). In English, the tricky part is usually the '-s'. For nouns, '-s' means Plural (Boys). But for verbs, '-s' means Singular (He plays). This is the opposite! Also, complex sentences with words like 'everyone', 'team', or 'neither/nor' have special rules that can be confusing. We will master them together!
contrastiveExplanation:
Let's look at the main differences between French and English agreement.

The Third Person '-s':
In English Present Simple, he/she/it takes an '-s' on the verb. I play, You play, We play... but He plays.
Error: "My brother like football." ❌ -> "My brother likes football." ✅

Intervening Phrases:
Sometimes words come between the subject and the verb. You must ignore them.
Example: "The box of chocolates is heavy." (The subject is BOX, not chocolates).
French speakers sometimes agree with the closest noun.

'People' and 'Police':
In French, 'le monde' is singular. In English, 'people' is plural.
French: "Les gens sont..." (Plural) / "Tout le monde est..." (Singular).
English: "People are..." (Always plural).

'News' and 'Information':
'News' ends in 's' but is singular. 'Information' has no 's' and is singular.
French: "Les nouvelles sont bonnes." (Plural).
English: "The news is good." (Singular).

commonErrors.wrong: My father work in a bank.
commonErrors.correct: My father works in a bank.
commonErrors.frenchConnection: Forgetting the '-s' for he/she/it is the most common error.

commonErrors.wrong: The people in this room is happy.
commonErrors.correct: The people in this room are happy.
commonErrors.frenchConnection: 'People' translates to 'gens' (plural) but learners often treat it as singular because it looks singular.
"Les nouvelles" is plural in French. In English, 'news' is an uncountable singular noun.
"Tout le monde" implies many people, but grammatically it is singular in both languages. English 'Everyone' takes a singular verb.
"La police" is singular in French. In English, 'police' is a collective plural noun.

items.questionText: My sister ___ to the market every Saturday.
items.feedback: Correct! 'My sister' is singular (she), so we add '-es' to the verb.
Correct! 'Students' is plural, so we use 'are'.
Correct! For he/she/it, we use the auxiliary 'does'.
Correct! 'Ngono and Muna' are two people (they), so the subject is plural.
Correct! The subject 'dog' is singular, so the verb needs an '-s'.

items.questionText: I ___ a student at the university.
items.feedback: Correct! The subject 'I' always goes with 'am'.
Correct! 'Parents' is plural (they), so we use the base verb 'live'.
Correct! The subject is 'brother' (he), so we start the question with 'Does'.
Correct! 'That car' is singular (it), so the verb needs an '-s'.
Correct! The subject 'We' takes 'have'.

items.questionText: The baby ___ when he is hungry.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Baby' is singular. Verbs ending in 'y' change to 'ies'.
Correct! 'You' always takes 'are', even if it is one person.

items.questionText: It ___ heavily in the rainy season.
items.feedback: Correct! The subject 'It' is singular, so we add '-s'.

items.questionText: The teachers ___ in the staff room.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Teachers' is plural, so we use 'are'.
Correct! 'She' is singular. Verbs ending in 'sh' take '-es'.
Correct! 'Cars' is plural, so we use the base verb 'pass'.
Correct! 'Uncle' is singular (he), so we use 'has'.
Correct! 'Birds' is plural, so we use the base verb 'fly'.
Correct! The sun is singular, so we add '-s'.
Correct! The subject 'They' takes 'do'.

items.questionText: The box of chocolates ___ on the table.
items.feedback: Correct! The subject is 'The box' (singular). 'Of chocolates' is just extra information.
Correct! Indefinite pronouns like 'Everyone', 'Everyone', and 'Nobody' are singular in English.

items.questionText: There ___ many people at the market.
items.feedback: Correct! With 'There is/are', we look at the word AFTER the verb. 'People' is plural, so we use 'are'.

items.questionText: One of my friends ___ a doctor.
items.feedback: Correct! The subject is 'One' (singular), not 'friends'. One is a doctor.

items.questionText: Bread and butter ___ my favourite breakfast.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Bread and butter' is considered one single meal/idea, so it is singular.

items.questionText: The police ___ searching for the thief.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Police' is a collective noun that is always plural in English.

items.questionText: Ten kilometers ___ a long distance to walk.
items.feedback: Correct! Distances, money, and time periods are treated as singular units.

items.questionText: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ here.
items.feedback: Correct! With 'Neither...nor', the verb agrees with the noun closest to it. 'Students' is plural, so we use 'are'.
Correct! 'News' ends in 's', but it is an uncountable singular noun.
Correct! 'Someone' is an indefinite pronoun and is always singular.
Correct! The subject is 'shoes' (plural). In questions, the verb comes first, but it must still agree with the subject.
Correct! 'Water' is uncountable. With 'All of...', we look at the noun. Uncountable nouns take singular verbs.
Correct! The subject is the action 'Making' (gerund), which is singular. 'Friends' is the object, not the subject.
Correct! Subject names ending in 's' (Mathematics, Physics, Economics) are singular.

items.questionText: The people in my village ___ very friendly.
items.feedback: Correct! 'People' is always plural.

items.questionText: Either the pen or the book ___ on the desk.
items.feedback: Correct! With 'Either...or', we agree with the closest noun. 'Book' is singular.
Correct! In sentences starting with 'Here' or 'There', the subject comes after the verb. 'The bus' is singular.

items.questionText: A lot of students ___ absent today.
items.feedback: Correct! With 'A lot of', we look at the noun. 'Students' is countable and plural.
Correct! Collective nouns (team, family, class) are usually singular when acting as one group.

items.questionText: The quality of the mangoes ___ poor.
items.feedback: Correct! The subject is 'Quality' (singular), not 'mangoes'.
Correct! 'The number' refers to a specific statistic/figure, so it is singular.
Correct! 'A number of' means 'many' or 'several', so it is plural.

items.questionText: Neither the students nor the teacher ___ happy about the exam.
items.feedback: Correct! Proximity rule: We agree with 'the teacher' (singular) because it is closer to the verb.

items.questionText: The poor ___ help from the government.
items.feedback: Correct! Adjectives used as nouns (The poor, The rich, The blind) refer to a group of people and are always plural.

items.questionText: Each of the girls ___ a prize.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Each' is distributive and singular. Ignore 'of the girls'.

items.questionText: Ten thousand francs ___ too much for that shirt.
items.feedback: Correct! Amounts of money are treated as a singular unit.
Correct! Tools with two parts (scissors, glasses, trousers) are plural.

items.questionText: A pair of scissors ___ on the table.
items.feedback: Correct! Here the subject is 'A pair' (singular), not 'scissors'.
Correct! Diseases ending in 's' (Measles, Mumps, Diabetes) are singular.

items.questionText: Not only the students but also the teacher ___ tired.
items.feedback: Correct! With 'Not only... but also', the verb agrees with the closest subject (the teacher).
Correct! With fractions/percentages, we look at the noun. 'Mangoes' is plural.

items.questionText: Half of the population ___ in cities.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Population' is a collective singular noun. Half of a singular whole is singular.

items.questionText: Either you or I ___ going to drive.
items.feedback: Correct! Proximity rule. The verb agrees with 'I'. It sounds strange, but 'or I am' is correct.
Correct! 'Cattle' looks singular but is always plural.
Correct! The expression 'Many a...' is followed by a singular noun and singular verb. It means 'many', but structurally it is singular.

items.questionText: The committee ___ divided on the issue.
items.feedback: Correct! Usually collective nouns are singular, but when the members disagree or act individually, we use the plural.
Correct! 'More than one' is followed by a singular noun and singular verb.

items.questionText: Identifying the errors in these sentences ___ difficult.
items.feedback: Correct! The subject is the gerund phrase 'Identifying the errors'. The phrase acts as a singular 'It'.
Correct! Clauses starting with 'What' are typically singular.

items.questionText: There ___ a pen and two books on the desk.
items.feedback: Correct! When 'There' is followed by a list, the verb agrees with the *first* item in the list (a pen).
Correct! 'My brother' is singular (he), so we add '-s'.

items.questionText: The dogs ___ running in the park.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Dogs' is plural, so we use 'are'.
Correct! For she, we use the auxiliary 'does'.
Correct! While often a dish, here we are talking about two separate ingredients, so plural 'are' is safer, though 'is' is possible if it's a specific dish name. Let's assume two items here.

items.questionText: Red beans and rice ___ a popular dish.

items.questionText: Two hours ___ enough time to finish the exam.

items.questionText: Neither Muna nor his brothers ___ at the party.

items.questionText: Either the bags or the box ___ heavy.
items.feedback: Correct! Agree with 'box' (singular) because it is closer.
Correct! Subject 'The teacher' is singular.
Correct! 'Some of' + plural count noun = plural verb.
Correct! 'Family' is a collective noun, treated as one unit here.

items.questionText: The colour of the flowers ___ beautiful.
items.feedback: Correct! Subject is 'Colour' (singular).

items.questionText: The number of cars on the road ___ increased.
items.feedback: Correct! 'The number' is singular.
Correct! 'A number of' is plural.

items.questionText: Neither the players nor the coach ___ ready.
items.feedback: Correct! Agree with 'coach' (singular).
Correct! 'The rich' means 'rich people' (plural).

items.questionText: Each of the houses ___ a garage.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Each' is singular.

items.questionText: Five million dollars ___ a lot of money.
items.feedback: Correct! Money amount is singular.
Correct! 'Glasses' (for eyes) is plural.

items.questionText: A pair of trousers ___ in the wardrobe.
items.feedback: Correct! Subject is 'A pair' (singular).
Correct! 'Economics' is a subject name, so it is singular.

items.questionText: Not only the mother but also her children ___ sick.
items.feedback: Correct! Agree with 'children' (plural) as it is closer.
Correct! 'Students' is plural, so half of them is plural.
Correct! 'Cake' is singular. Half of it is singular.

items.questionText: Either she or I ___ to blame.
items.feedback: Correct! Proximity rule. Agree with 'I'.

items.questionText: The cattle ___ moved to a new field.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Cattle' is plural.

items.questionText: Many a man ___ tried to climb that mountain.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Many a man' takes a singular verb.
Correct! They are acting individually (arguing), so we use the plural.
Correct! 'More than one' takes a singular noun and verb.
Correct! Subject is the gerund 'Learning'.
Correct! The clause 'What he says' is a singular subject.

items.questionText: There ___ a book and a pen on the table.
items.feedback: Correct! In 'There is/are', agree with the FIRST item in the list.
